definitions.gloss: Kōbō Daishi; the posthumous title of Kūkai
definitions.explanation: The title the imperial court gave the monk Kūkai (774–835), founder of Shingon Buddhism, in 921, long after his death. It is the name by which most people know him.

examples.japanese: {弘法大師|こうぼうだいし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{空海|くうかい}→空海：31131_kuukai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ことだ。
{弘法大師|こうぼうだいし}⟦ゆかり→ゆかり：10650_yukari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{巡|めぐ}る→巡る：03930_meguru⟧。
examples.english: To make a round of temples associated with Kōbō Daishi.

examples.japanese: ⟦{四国|しこく}→四国：21447_shikoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{八十八|はちじゅうはっ}か{所|しょ}{巡|めぐ}り⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{弘法大師|こうぼうだいし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{足跡|そくせき}→足跡：26262_sokuseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧たどる⟦{巡礼|じゅんれい}→巡礼：10662_junrei⟧だ。
examples.english: The Shikoku 88-temple circuit is a pilgrimage that follows in Kōbō Daishi's footsteps.

notes:
Among believers he is affectionately called お{大師|だいし}さま.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}り→弘法も筆の誤り：29266_kouboumofudenoayamari⟧: even Kōbō slips with the brush (anyone can make a mistake)
- {弘法|こうぼう}⟦{筆|ふで}→筆：03601_fude⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ば→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧ず: Kōbō does not choose his brush (a master does not blame the tools)

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Legends of springs and wells he opened are told all over Japan
- The ⟦{お遍路|おへんろ}→お遍路：19059_ohenro⟧ pilgrimage in Shikoku walks in his footsteps; pilgrims' hats carry the words {同行二人|どうぎょうににん} ("two traveling together": the pilgrim and Kōbō Daishi)
